extra_misconceptions.fact: Heat or suffocation causes the tick to regurgitate infectious fluids into the wound; grasp it near the skin with fine tweezers and pull up.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burning an attached tick with a match or coating it in petroleum jelly forces it to back out safely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Incising or sucking a snakebite damages blood vessels and introduces bacteria; keep the victim calm, immobilize the limb, and get medical help.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting a snakebite wound and sucking out the venom reduces the amount of toxin entering the bloodstream.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Squeezing the venom sac injects more toxin into the skin; scrape the stinger sideways using the edge of a credit card or dull knife blade.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pinching a bee stinger between your thumb and forefinger is the fastest way to stop venom injection.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gulping cold water can trigger severe stomach cramps and vomiting; move the person to shade, cool the skin, and give small sips of water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drinking a large bottle of ice water all at once is the safest treatment for a surveyor with heat exhaustion.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to embedded mouthparts if you twist or squeeze an attached tick instead of pulling straight up with fine tweezers?
Which physical indicator distinguishes life-threatening heatstroke from heat exhaustion during an afternoon boundary survey?
Why is it dangerous to apply a tourniquet or cut and suck venom after a venomous snakebite in a remote survey brushline?
Where should a rod person inspect on a wooden stake or brush line before clearing a sightline in copperhead and poison ivy habitat?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Adjusting leveling screws tilts the vertical axis slightly; always recheck and recenter the optical plummet or plumb bob after final leveling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leveling the transit head with the leveling screws automatically keeps the optical plummet centered over the corner tack.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Boundary plats require horizontal distances; surveyors must either hold the tape level with a plumb bob or apply a slope angle correction.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling a survey tape along the ground slope gives the true horizontal distance required for boundary calculations.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Erasing destroys original legal evidence in a field book; cross out errors with a single line and write the corrected value neatly above it.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Erasing a mistaken distance in the field notebook keeps legal survey records cleaner and more accurate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A range pole held out of plumb shifts the line of sight horizontally; always sight the lowest visible point near the tack or plumb the pole.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sighting the top of a tilted range pole yields the same horizontal angle as sighting the bottom tip on the corner tack.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to every recorded horizontal angle if the tripod shifts or loses center over the occupied corner hub mid-survey?
Which field check at the end of a radial round confirms that the theodolite horizontal circle did not slip on the tripod head?
Under what condition does a sloped steel tape measurement overestimate the true horizontal distance between two lot corners?
Why is it dangerous to erase an erroneous angle entry in a surveyor's field book instead of lining it out with a single stroke?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Photocopying or resizing changes paper dimensions and invalidates written ratios, whereas a drawn graphic scale bar shrinks proportionally.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A written scale statement such as 1 inch equals 30 feet remains accurate even when a plat is photocopied at a reduced size.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Survey distances are recorded in decimal feet, requiring an engineer's scale graduated in multiples of ten units per inch for accurate plotting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Measuring decimal feet on a plat with a standard 16ths-of-an-inch ruler produces exact engineering scale lengths.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All radial angles were turned from a single instrument station, so the protractor must stay centered on that station aligned to the baseline.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Radial angles recorded from a reference corner are plotted by moving the protractor center to each newly drawn perimeter point.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Magnetic north differs from true north by the local magnetic declination angle, so a survey plat must note which north reference is shown.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Magnetic north and true geodetic north point in the exact same direction on a property survey map.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the plotted position of a distant lot corner if your protractor baseline is off by even one degree at the station?
Why is a graphic scale bar essential on a boundary plat even when a written ratio like 1 inch equals 20 feet is printed on the page?
Where should the protractor index center and zero-degree baseline align when plotting radial angles turned from your reference line?
Which distinction separates an engineer's scale divided into tenths of an inch from a standard architect's fractional inch ruler?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Height of Instrument is the elevation of the level line of sight, calculated by adding the benchmark elevation and the backsight rod reading.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Height of Instrument in differential leveling is found by measuring from the ground beneath the tripod up to the telescope eyepiece.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Because the level sightline stays fixed above the rod, a larger foresight reading means the ground dropped further below the line of sight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A larger foresight reading on the leveling rod indicates that the sighted corner stake sits at a higher ground elevation.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Any forward or backward tilt makes the rod a hypotenuse, causing the crosshair to read a higher number than the true vertical height.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tilting the leveling rod slightly away from the instrument makes the crosshair reading smaller than the true vertical height.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Survey leveling rods are graduated in feet, tenths, and hundredths of a foot so elevations can be added and subtracted using decimal arithmetic.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Philadelphia leveling rods are graduated in feet and twelve inches just like a carpenter's tape measure.

extra_socratic_questions: What calculation determines the Height of Instrument after sighting the leveling rod held on the 100-foot benchmark?
Why does reading a higher number on the Philadelphia rod mean the ground corner marker is actually at a lower elevation?
What happens to the rod reading if the rod person tilts the leveling rod forward or backward instead of holding it strictly plumb?
Which field procedure at the end of a level loop verifies that no rod reading blunders or tripod settlement occurred during the run?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Street addresses and tax numbers are only for mail and assessment; the legal description of courses, monuments, or subdivision lots governs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A property's street address or tax parcel number in a deed is the legally binding definition of its boundary lines.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Under the legal hierarchy of evidence, undisturbed natural and artificial monuments called for in the deed control over bearings and distances.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Written distances and acreage numbers in a deed always override physical boundary monuments found in the ground.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An easement grants a specific right of use or access across the land while the property owner retains underlying title to the parcel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A utility easement recorded in a property deed transfers ownership of that strip of land to the utility company.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A quitclaim deed transfers only whatever interest the grantor currently possesses, whereas a warranty deed guarantees clear title and defense.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A quitclaim deed guarantees that the grantor holds clear, unencumbered title and surveyed boundaries to the parcel.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the legal validity of a metes and bounds description if the perimeter calls fail to return to the Point of Beginning?
Which legal rule resolves a boundary conflict when a deed's written distance disagrees with an original iron monument?
What distinction separates a recorded Plat Lot and Block legal description from a traditional metes and bounds boundary description?
Why must a surveyor review utility and access easements listed in a deed even though easements do not transfer fee simple ownership?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Optical photogrammetry only maps visible top surfaces like leaves, whereas LiDAR laser pulses penetrate small canopy gaps to hit bare ground.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard drone camera photogrammetry can measure bare-earth ground elevations directly through a closed, leafy forest canopy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard autonomous drone GPS drifts by several feet; survey-grade accuracy requires Ground Control Points or RTK/PPK carrier-phase corrections.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Consumer drone GPS receivers alone achieve survey-grade centimeter accuracy without ground control points or RTK corrections.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Laser scanners are strictly line-of-sight instruments, so surveyors must register scans from multiple stations to eliminate shadow occlusions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A single terrestrial laser scanner setup can capture every wall and surface of a building without any blind spots.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Laser scanners only record surface geometry; locating buried ferrous monuments and interpreting legal title still require a ground surveyor.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dense 3D point clouds from laser scanners automatically identify buried iron boundary pins and legal property lines.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the elevation accuracy of an optical drone photogrammetry survey over dense forest canopy compared to airborne LiDAR?
Why must a surveyor establish surveyed Ground Control Points on the terrain before flying a photogrammetric mapping drone mission?
Under what site condition does a terrestrial 3D laser scanner require multiple overlapping setups to capture a complete structure?
Which regulatory and legal limitation prevents an aerial drone orthomosaic map from replacing a ground-monumented boundary survey?

extra_misconceptions.fact: GPS satellites are one-way broadcast beacons; ground receivers only listen to timed signals and compute position by trilateration.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Surveyors using GPS equipment transmit radio signals up to the satellites in orbit to request their ground coordinates.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A fourth satellite signal is mandatory to solve for the timing clock bias between the receiver's quartz clock and the satellite atomic clocks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Three GPS satellites are sufficient to determine exact latitude, longitude, and elevation on a standard survey receiver.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Consumer GPS reads coarse code signals accurate to several meters, while survey RTK receivers track carrier-wave phase for centimeter accuracy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Handheld hiking GPS units and survey-grade RTK GNSS rovers use the same signal measurement method and achieve identical accuracy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Satellites bunched together create poor geometry and high PDOP error; wide angular separation across the sky yields the strongest 3D position.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Closely clustered satellites directly overhead provide better geometric dilution of precision than satellites spread across the sky.

extra_socratic_questions: Why does a GPS receiver require simultaneous signals from at least four satellites instead of three to solve a 3D survey position?
What happens to RTK GNSS accuracy when a rover operates next to tall metal buildings or under heavy overhead tree canopy?
Which physical error source does a stationary RTK base station measure and broadcast to the rover to achieve centimeter precision?
Where does a GPS satellite range signal travel compared to an optical total station sightline between two mountain valley corners?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Establishing legal property boundaries is restricted by state law to licensed Professional Land Surveyors who have passed state boundary exams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any licensed civil engineer is legally authorized to monument property boundaries and stamp subdivision plats in every state.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Passing the FS exam earns Surveyor-in-Training status; full licensure requires years of supervised experience plus the PS and state exams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passing the NCEES Fundamentals of Surveying exam immediately grants a surveyor a full license to sign and seal boundary surveys.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern surveyors blend field robotics and drone flight with CAD drafting, GIS database management, courthouse title research, and boundary law.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern surveying careers consist almost entirely of outdoor manual labor cutting brush and holding range poles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many technicians enter as paid rod or instrument operators through technical colleges or apprenticeships while working toward full licensure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-year college degree is the only pathway to enter the surveying profession and earn an income in the field.

extra_socratic_questions: What legal authority distinguishes a licensed Professional Land Surveyor from an unlicensed survey field technician?
Which examination and field apprenticeship milestones must a graduate complete after passing the Fundamentals of Surveying exam?
Where do hydrographic, geodetic, and construction layout surveyors differ in the primary measurements and clients they serve?
Why do states require licensed land surveyors to carry errors and omissions liability insurance and complete continuing education?
